sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Edmonson County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
The county's tax offices are all in or near the courthouse in Brownsville, the county seat and its only municipality. The Property Valuation Administrator (PVA) values parcels from the Edmonson County Courthouse on Main Cross Street at 270-597-2381. The Edmonson County Sheriff collects the bills at 110 Jackson Street, 270-597-2157, and the County Clerk keeps the land records and takes delinquent bills at 108 North Main Street, 270-597-2624.

County government posts weekday hours of 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., and its own welcome page jokes that the county does not have a single stoplight. The PVA links a qPublic parcel search from its website, which is the quickest way to see how a house is assessed before calling anyone.

Neither the PVA nor the sheriff decides how much tax a district raises. Value comes from the PVA, and the levy comes from the bodies that set rates, which in Edmonson County include the fiscal court and the county school system. Ask the sheriff's office for the combined rate that applies to a given parcel.

sections.h2: When are Edmonson County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
The Edmonson County Sheriff runs a schedule that starts later than the state's default, because bills go out on October 30. Anyone without a bill by November 15 should call the sheriff for a duplicate, which is mailed promptly. Under KRS 134.015, when collection starts late the Department of Revenue may set an alternative schedule that gives a month to each stage, and the sheriff's calendar follows that pattern.

Edmonson County Sheriff collection calendar for property and tangible tax bills
Payment windowAmount due
Through November 30Face amount less 2 percent
December 1 to December 31Face amount
January 1 to January 31Face amount plus 5 percent
February 1 to April 15Face amount plus 21 percent

The 21 percent after January reflects a 10 percent penalty and a 10 percent sheriff's add-on, which the state's property tax calendar lists for payments after January 31. Bills still unpaid at the close of business on April 15 move to the County Clerk.

The sheriff's office takes cash in person, checks, money orders and major credit cards by phone or at the counter, with processing fees on cards. Counter hours run 7:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Friday, 7:30 a.m. to noon on Thursday, and 7:30 a.m. to noon on Saturday. Mail goes to the same Jackson Street address.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Edmonson County assessment?
sections.html:
Begin with a conference at the PVA's office during the tax roll inspection period, then file with the County Clerk if the two sides do not agree. Real property is valued as of January 1 each year and can be listed with the PVA from January 1 through March 1. Personal property, such as business equipment, has until May 15.

  • The roll is open for 13 days beginning the first Monday in May, six days a week including Saturday.
  • A conference with the PVA or a deputy must come before any appeal, and the owner then has until close of business on the next workday after inspection ends to file with the clerk.
  • The local board of assessment appeals meets 25 to 35 days after the inspection period closes and sits for five days at most unless the state grants more time.
  • An appeal needs evidence: land and building details, insurance policies, construction costs or sale listings. Without them the board denies the appeal.
  • Missing the board hearing ends the owner's right to go on to the Kentucky Claims Commission.

If tax bills are printed before an appeal ends, the owner's stated opinion of value is used, and a supplemental bill follows should the final value come out higher.

sections.h2: How much does the homestead exemption save in Edmonson County?
sections.html:
It lowers the taxable value of a qualifying home by $49,100 for the 2025 and 2026 assessment years. Homeowners qualify at age 65 or if classified as totally disabled, and the application is filed with the Edmonson County PVA.

Take a house worth the county's Census median of $160,300. After the exemption, the taxable value drops to $111,200, so the owner pays tax on roughly 31 percent less value. Age can be proved with a birth certificate, driver's license or passport. A disability claim needs classification under a federal or retirement system program and disability payments for the whole assessment period, and it must be renewed each year unless the owner is a veteran with a service-connected disability or has been found totally and permanently disabled by Social Security or the Kentucky Retirement Systems.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell an Edmonson County house with unpaid taxes?
sections.html:
The taxes stay with the property and become a lien. KRS 134.015 makes the tax a personal debt of the owner on the assessment date, and the lien on delinquent property lasts until payment or the 11-year period in KRS 134.420 runs out, whoever owns the house. A title search at closing will show it.

After April 15 the County Clerk holds the bill as a certificate of delinquency, and a lien is recorded. Interest of 1 percent per month starts, and the county attorney sends notices before the tax sale, which Kentucky schedules 90 to 135 days after the transfer. The clerk advertises the list in The Edmonson News. For the 2024 bills, the list ran on August 13, 2025, and the sale was held on September 16, 2025 at 11:00 a.m., with buyers required to register by September 5 and put down 25 percent of the certificates they wanted.

The clerk's notice also says that payments must be received in full before the sale date, and money that arrives afterward is returned. A bill may be pulled from the sale list under KRS 134.504. Call the clerk at 270-597-2624 for a payoff figure before listing.

At closing, the deed carries a state transfer tax of $0.50 per $500 of value, paid by the seller as grantor. On a $160,300 sale that comes to $160.50, and the clerk charges $33 to record a deed of up to five pages under KRS 64.012.

sections.h2: What is Edmonson County, Kentucky, like for a seller?
sections.html:
Edmonson County sits in south central Kentucky and was created on January 12, 1825 from parts of Grayson, Hart and Warren counties. It covers 308 square miles, of which 303 are land, and it lies in the Bowling Green metropolitan area. Mammoth Cave National Park takes up roughly a fourth of the county, and Nolin Lake State Park lies mostly in the north. The county is dry, and the courthouse built in 1873 replaced an earlier one whose floor collapsed.

Getting around means state routes. KY 70 crosses the county east to west, KY 259 meets KY 101 after the only Green River bridge in the county, and KY 185 links the west side with Bowling Green. I-65 clips the southeastern tip with no interchange inside the county. Edmonson County Schools runs five schools, including the high school and middle school complex in Brownsville. Census QuickFacts reports:

  • Population: 12,749 in 2025, up 5.1 percent since the 2020 base.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 80.1 percent, across 5,099 households.
  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $160,300.
  • Median gross rent: $778; median household income: $54,937.
  • Mean travel time to work: 32.9 minutes.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher: 10.7 percent of adults.

The long commute and large share of homeowners mean most sales are of older, owner-occupied houses. A seller dealing with back taxes or repairs can ask the sheriff and clerk for exact balances, then compare a conventional listing with an as-is cash sale.

faqs.q: When does the Edmonson County tax discount end?
faqs.a: The 2 percent discount ends on November 30 under the sheriff's calendar, because bills are mailed October 30. The base amount is due December 1 through December 31, and a 5 percent penalty applies in January.

faqs.q: Where do I pay property tax in Edmonson County?
faqs.a: Pay at the Edmonson County Sheriff's Office, 110 Jackson Street in Brownsville, or mail a check or money order to that address. The counter takes cash, and cards are accepted by phone or in person with a processing fee.

faqs.q: Who sets my Edmonson County property value?
faqs.a: The Edmonson County PVA sets it, using January 1 as the valuation date. The office is in the courthouse and can be reached at 270-597-2381; the sheriff and fiscal court have no say in the value.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Edmonson County assessment later in the year?
faqs.a: No. Appeals start with a PVA conference during the 13-day inspection period that begins the first Monday in May, and the filing at the clerk's office closes the next workday after that period ends.

faqs.q: What does Edmonson County do with unpaid property taxes?
faqs.a: Unpaid bills move to the County Clerk after April 15 as certificates of delinquency and collect 1 percent monthly interest. The clerk advertises them in late summer and holds a tax sale, and payments must reach the clerk in full before the sale date.
